## Sparse color-2 points connected by a minimum Manhattan network

Evidence: task-29d679dc (demo 1 and solved test, 2026-11-02). A zero grid contains several isolated color-2 markers. Output preserves all marker cells and joins them with color 3 using a rectilinear median spine:

1. List marker row and column coordinates (zero-based).
2. Choose the median row of the marker rows as the horizontal spine. With an even number of markers, the middle rows may coincide or form a range; observed examples use the row that makes a median horizontal spine (when test had six markers, middle rows were both 8; demo had marker rows 3,6,6,9,11, median row 6).
3. Fill color 3 horizontally between the minimum and maximum marker columns along the spine, retaining any marker-2 cells on that row.
4. For each marker not on the spine, fill color 3 vertically in that marker's column from the marker toward the spine, retaining the marker itself as 2. Keep all unrelated cells 0.
5. Validate output dimensions and each row length carefully before submitting.

Solved test coordinates (14x17): (3,6),(6,4),(8,1),(8,12),(10,10),(12,8). Spine row 8, horizontal span columns 1..12; vertical branches at columns 6,4,10,8. This exactly matched the correct output.

Demo coordinates (19x13): (3,8),(6,4),(6,12),(9,10),(11,7). Median spine row 6, span columns 4..12; branches at columns 8,10,7. Demo output confirms connecting all markers by those vertical branches and the horizontal span. The rule is consistent with Manhattan median/rectilinear network construction; retain original 2s and color only connecting cells 3.
